_about: The Herald's deck: original Solos Gems tables the quest Dungeon Master draws from at random (see handleQuest in worker.js). Classic quest shapes (the false friend, the bargain with a price, the prize that is not what it seems) inspired by public-domain myth and romance; all wording is our own. The legends table retells motifs from public-domain myth, folklore and literature (Arthurian romance, Homer, Grimm, the Arabian Nights, Norse and Celtic tales) in our own words.
twists: The person who hired the hero is the one who caused the problem, and they would very much like that to stay quiet.
The monster everyone fears is guarding something, not hoarding it, and it has been doing a genuinely good job.
The treasure is real, but it is also alive, and it has opinions about who should own it.
Two factions both want the prize for opposite reasons, and both are a little bit right.
The map the hero is following was drawn by someone who has never been here and lied about it with great confidence.
A helpful stranger turns out to be the villain's accountant, who is having a crisis of conscience.
The curse can be lifted, but only by doing the most embarrassing thing anyone in the village can imagine.
The villain's plan is already finished. What remains is the much harder job of undoing it.
The prophecy everyone keeps quoting was mistranslated. It says 'a hero shall arrive with snacks,' not 'a hero shall arrive with swords.'
The door everyone has been trying to open was never locked. It was just stuck, and also slightly afraid.
The 'ancient evil' is a junior wizard who started a spell three hundred years ago and has been too embarrassed to stop it.
The reward on offer was already promised to four other adventurers, who are all on their way.
What looked like a rescue is actually a heist, and the hero is the getaway cart.
The villain sincerely believes they are the hero, and keeps leaving the hero helpful, slightly condescending notes.
The guide knows the way perfectly, but charges by the hour and has made the route very scenic.
The real danger is not the dragon. It is the dragon's landlord.
An item the hero picked up earlier turns out to matter enormously, and someone dangerous now knows they have it.
The town the hero is saving would honestly prefer to be left alone with its problem, which it has grown attached to.
Someone has been impersonating the hero, and they have been doing a much better job of it.
The magic stops working in this place for a reason that is petty, specific and entirely the hero's fault.
A bargain offered earlier comes due, and the price is not gold. It is a favor, owed to someone who keeps a very good ledger.
The ally is completely loyal, but to the job, not to the hero, and the job just changed.
The final room is a waiting room. The villain is running late.
The thing being hunted has been hunting the hero back, and it is winning on points.
The quest's goal turns out to be a symbol. The real prize is a person who has been in plain sight the whole time.
Everyone in the tavern is secretly part of the same guild, and the hero just insulted its founder.
The weapon that can defeat the villain exists, but it is currently being used as a doorstop by someone who loves it.
Time moves differently past the next door: an hour inside is a week outside, and rent is due.
The villain can be beaten easily. The problem is that their much worse sibling is next in line.
The hero's own past catches up with them in the form of a very specific, very angry goose.
A rival adventurer arrives, better equipped and worse at everything, and insists on helping.
The innocent captive has quietly been running the dungeon from the inside for years.
What everyone thought was a ghost is a perfectly alive person nobody ever bothered to notice.
The wishes are real. They are just processed by a committee.
The bridge back home has been taken down for repairs, scheduled to finish never.
characters: a retired knight who now works the toll booth and narrates every coin he receives
a goblin with a clipboard who believes, correctly, that the paperwork is the real dungeon
a nervous oracle who only predicts things that happened last Tuesday
a cheerful necromancer running a skeleton staffing agency
a bard who is extremely famous in one very small village
a dragon in the middle of a midlife crisis, considering a career in pottery
a talking crow who works on commission and lies only about the weather
an innkeeper who has seen everything and is unimpressed by all of it
a paladin who is deeply committed to an oath he has partly forgotten
a witch who answers every question with a recipe
a troll who charges a riddle to cross the bridge and has run out of riddles
a sentient suit of armor looking for someone to fill it, emotionally
a merchant selling maps of places that do not exist yet
a tax collector for a kingdom that fell a century ago, still on the job
a minotaur who just wants someone to admire the maze he designed
a halfling cook who settles every argument with soup
a vampire who is very polite about the whole blood situation
a wizard's apprentice left in charge for 'one afternoon' four years ago
a lich who keeps their phylactery in a jar labeled 'definitely not my soul'
a mimic who has been a chest so long it is unsure how to be anything else
an elf who is three thousand years old and still bad at small talk
a dwarven auditor who can smell an unbalanced ledger from across a mountain
a ghost who haunts the place out of habit and would love a hobby
a gnome inventor whose inventions all work perfectly, just not at what they were built for
a mercenary who is fiercely loyal to whoever fed them most recently
a cult leader having serious second thoughts about the whole prophecy thing
a royal food taster who has become extremely brave and extremely suspicious
an orc poet working on an epic and looking for a heroic subject
a fairy who grants favors but files them in triplicate
a stable hand who is the only person who knows what is actually going on
complications: Someone important is watching, and they are taking notes.
The way back is suddenly blocked, so the only direction left is forward.
A storm, a fire or a flood arrives at the worst possible moment.
The hero's best item fails right when it is needed, for a funny reason.
An innocent bystander gets swept up and refuses to leave.
The clock is now ticking: something bad happens if the hero takes too long.
A rival grabs the same clue at the same moment.
The local law arrives and has questions, mostly about the hero's paperwork.
A favor someone did for the hero earlier now needs repaying, right now.
Something the hero said earlier was overheard and repeated, badly.
An animal takes a strong liking to the hero and will not be separated from them.
The ground, the floor or the ceiling has become unreliable.
A celebration breaks out nearby, making everything louder and more crowded.
The villain sends a messenger with a very reasonable offer.
A secret door opens onto something the hero was not ready for.
The hero's reputation arrives before them, and it has been exaggerated.
A small mistake from earlier snowballs into a medium-sized catastrophe.
A deal goes wrong because both sides were lying, in different directions.
The light source runs out.
Someone the hero helped earlier shows up to return the favor, unhelpfully.
oddities: a compass that points toward whatever you are most avoiding
a key that fits every lock, but only on Tuesdays
a sword that sings, badly, whenever it is drawn
a bag of holding that has been holding someone else's lunch for decades
a cloak of invisibility that only works when nobody is looking
a potion labeled 'probably healing'
a scroll of fireball written by someone who could not spell fireball
a crown that makes the wearer feel important and nothing else
a mirror that shows you what you looked like yesterday
a ring of three wishes, two already used, with a note: 'sorry'
a lantern that only lights up things that want to be seen
a pair of boots that walk home on their own if you fall asleep
a lucky coin that is extremely unlucky for whoever you give it to
a quill that writes the truth, in very small handwriting
a shield with a face that offers unsolicited tactical advice
an hourglass that runs faster when you are having fun
a teapot that brews whatever the holder needs to hear
a rope that ties itself into knots when it is nervous
a deck of cards where every card is the same card, and it is judging you
a map of the dungeon drawn by the dungeon itself, which is biased
a horn that summons help, in the form of one confused farmer
a gem that glows near danger and also near cheese
a dagger that returns when thrown, slightly offended
a cursed amulet whose curse is mostly bad puns
a jar containing a small, very polite storm
places: a tavern built inside the ribcage of something enormous
a library where the books reshelve themselves out of spite
a market that only exists between midnight and one in the morning
a bridge with a toll, a troll, and a surprisingly strict dress code
a castle that rearranges its rooms whenever it gets bored
a swamp with excellent acoustics
a monastery of monks who have taken a vow of sarcasm
an abandoned wizard tower where the spells are still running unattended
a mine where the dwarves dug too deep and found an extremely tidy basement
a floating island that drifts over a different kingdom every night
a graveyard where the residents hold weekly meetings
a forest where the trees gossip about travelers
an underground city lit entirely by glowing mushrooms with strong opinions
a lighthouse that guides ships toward danger on purpose, for a good reason
a royal court where everyone is pretending the king is not a cat
a desert caravan inn that is somehow always the next dune over
a frozen lake with something warm and patient beneath it
a guildhall for heroes, with a long waiting list and worse coffee
a crossroads where a different signpost lies each time you look
a palace made of glass, where nobody can keep a secret
schemes: quietly buying up every bridge in the region, one toll at a time
replacing the town council with very convincing scarecrows
collecting forgotten names to power an old and hungry spell
rewriting the kingdom's history books so they come out as the hero
draining the magic out of a sacred spring to sell by the bottle
training an army of extremely obedient geese
arranging a royal wedding that ends with them on the throne
waking something ancient that they are sure they can control
stealing everyone's luck, a little at a time, through rigged dice games
flooding the market with fake magic items to ruin the wizards' guild
convincing the dragon that the town owes it rent
building a tower tall enough to argue with the sky
kidnapping every bard so nobody can sing about what they did
turning the season to permanent winter to corner the firewood market
trading the town's future to a fey lord for a single perfect afternoon
legends: A green-skinned stranger offers a beheading game: strike me once now, and I strike you once in a year.
The hero escapes a one-eyed giant by giving a false name, and later regrets bragging about the real one.
Three impossible tasks set by a jealous ruler, each solved with help from a creature the hero was kind to earlier.
A hut on chicken legs that only turns its door toward guests who ask politely.
A djinn grants wishes literally, and very much enjoys the loopholes.
Fairy food that traps anyone who eats it in the fair folk's court for a hundred years.
A sword in a stone that refuses everyone who wants it too badly.
A labyrinth whose monster is less dangerous than its architect.
A trickster god who helps and hinders in equal measure and always wants a share.
A ship of the dead that collects promises left unkept.
A sleeping king under the hill who will wake only when the land truly needs him, and is grumpy about it.
A forbidden book that whispers the reader's name and knows things it should not.
A town where it is always the same day, and only the hero notices.
Seven-league boots that cover huge distances but cannot stop easily.
A golden apple marked 'for the fairest' thrown into a party to start a feud.
A bargain at the crossroads at midnight, with a price hidden in the wording.
A swan maiden whose feathered cloak was stolen, and who wants it back very badly.
A city of brass in the desert, empty but still perfectly polished.
A gingerbread house whose owner is extremely hospitable for suspicious reasons.
An ancient sorcerer-king sealed beneath a lake, slowly bribing the fish.
A princess who must be made to laugh, and every jester who failed is now a statue.
A ferryman across a dark river who must be paid, and remembers anyone who cheats.
A tower with no door, entered only by climbing someone's very long hair.
A monster that can only be beaten by showing it its own reflection.
A magic mill at the bottom of the sea that grinds out salt forever.
A thief who steals the sound of a cat's footsteps and the roots of a mountain to forge a chain.
A knight sworn to answer one riddle: what do people most desire?
A dragon sleeping on a hoard, woken by a single stolen cup.
A pied piper who was never paid and has come back to collect.
A wandering city that walks on giant legs and stops for no one.
